# engram

> A single-binary terminal UI for the memories Claude Code writes to `~/.claude`,
> with team sharing over plain git. Free and open source under the MIT License.

Claude Code writes notes to itself as you work: what a project does, how you like
things, decisions you've made. They land as Markdown under `~/.claude`, one folder per project.
engram browses all of them in one two-pane TUI, and promotes the team-useful ones into a
git repository your teammates already have access to. No engram service or account:
your git host is the auth.

Claude Code shares team-written instructions through `CLAUDE.md` in the project repo,
but its auto-learned memories are machine-local. engram lets you promote selected
auto-learned memories through your own git remote.

- Install (Homebrew): `brew install ertugrulhaskan/tap/engram`
- Install (Go): `go install github.com/ertugrulhaskan/engram@latest`
- Platforms: macOS and Linux. Windows binaries ship but are untested; use WSL.
- Assistants: alongside Claude Code's memories, engram lists these read-only. Per project:
  `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, Cursor rules
  (`.cursor/rules/*.mdc`) and Copilot's `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`. Globally:
  `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` and `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, read from the home folder. Projects are
  found under `~/.claude/projects/`, and a `scanRoots` config setting points engram at any
  other folder, so a repo never opened in Claude Code appears too. A project can also be
  handed to an assistant: `@` opens an interactive Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex or Copilot
  session, listing only the CLIs you have. No assistant exposes a memory API, so other
  sources arrive as local files first, export/import later.

- Team sharing: promote a memory into a git store your team already has, or several at once,
  marked with `space`, as a single commit and push. A project-scoped memory is keyed to the
  git remote. A project that has none takes a name you give it with `>alias`, which promote
  and pull then use until the project gains a remote. Either way it lands in teammates'
  memory folders when they pull. A global-scoped one
  is tied to no repo: it lives in the store and keeps every copy you already hold in step, in
  whichever project you keep it. Every promoted memory is scanned for secrets first, including
  credentials broken across lines by a soft wrap or a YAML block scalar. When both sides of a
  memory have moved, `>resolve` shows an inline line-by-line diff of your copy against the
  store's before it opens `$EDITOR`, so the merge starts from what actually differs.
